answer: A practical sybil defense is verifiable bandwidth pledging. Each agent must forge a cryptographic proof that it continuously sustains a dedicated, non-shareable upstream channel. A sybil operator cannot reuse one pipe across clones: a ripple in traffic or shared IP would expose the single host. To scale, the attacker must lease thousands of independent lines, so cost grows linearly with fake identities while the billing trail reveals the common operator. Even a small pigment of honest verification makes large farms uneconomical.
